# Sigyn: the stories first, then the spelling

The marks in **Sigyn** make the most sense standing next to the myths they have to carry. So the myths come first.

## The Stories That Carry the Name

**The Wife of Loki.** Snorri names her in the survey of the Æsir with his usual economy: Loki's wife is named Sigyn, and their son is Nari or Narfi.  That is the whole introduction — no father, no hall, no office.  The same catalogue gives Loki his other family: the giantess [[angrboda|Angrboða]], who bore him the wolf [[fenrir|Fenrir]], the World Serpent, and [[hel|Hel]].

**The Captive in the Grove of Kettles.** The seeress of Völuspá, the oldest and greatest poem of the Codex Regius, sees the punishment before it happens: a captive lying under the grove of kettles, something evil-minded in form like Loki — 'and there sits Sigyn, by no means happy about her husband.  Do you understand yet, or what more? 'The stanza is the whole of her eddic portrait, and it is enough: seated, sorrowing, and staying.

**The Flyting's Aftermath.** Lokasenna ends in a prose coda as brutal as anything in the corpus.  Loki, who has slandered every god and goddess at Ægir's feast, is caught and bound across three stones with the entrails of his son Nari, while his other son Narfi is turned into a wolf.  [[skadi|Skaði]] takes a venomous snake and fastens it above his face, so that the venom drips down.

## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Sigyn
- **ASCII form:** sigyn
- **Meaning:** "Victorious girl-friend"
- **Domain of influence:** Loyalty, Wife of Loki
- **Pantheon:** Norse
- **Classification:** Tier 2
- **Original script:** ᛋᛁᚴᚢᚾ
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 330 of 397

## The Name Travels

Sigyn's truest kin are inside the corpus itself.  She is the mirror of [[nanna|Nanna]] — the two wives of the Baldr catastrophe, one following her dead husband into the fire, the other staying beside her living one in the pit; devotion answered by death in the one, by endurance without end in the other.

## The Address It Earned

The temple of **Sigyn** stands at [/sites/sigyn/](/sites/sigyn/) — [lore](/sites/sigyn/lore/), [scholars](/sites/sigyn/scholars/), [patterns](/sites/sigyn/patterns/) — because a name carrying this much story deserves more than a parking page. The restoration keeps one feature the ASCII form drops. One is enough to matter, and the label says so plainly: Tier-2.
